messages:
mike: Heads up — after landing the mixed-quant kernel selector change, QA hit a regression: structured JSON outputs from our summarization eval are sometimes malformed (missing keys or duplicated fields). Repro steps attached.
anya: ugh, saw a couple failing eval runs in the nightly. EMR/ROUGE deltas look small but behavior is non-deterministic which is worse. share repro?
sanjay: repro here: `run_local_eval --model redwood-mix-q4_k --quant-mode mixfp8-int8 --kv-cache enabled --batch 4 --seed 42`
claire: can you paste the broken example?
mike: here's one snippet from the eval that fails parsing (output should be JSON with title/body/metadata):
```
{"title":"Quarterly update","metadata": {"author":"ops"}, "body":"..."}
{"title":"Quarterly update","body":"...","body":"duplicate-body"
```
notice the duplicated body key in the bad run.
anya: interesting. duplicate keys smells like generation tokenization alignment / kv-cache replay bug rather than pure quant noise. but quant calibration can change logits enough to push to different tokens, so both plausible.
perf-bot: nightly-profile: model=redwood-mix-q4_k commit=ab12f3 kernel-selector=v2 -> p50 token latency +11%, p99 +9%, throughput -6%
mike: latency change is real, but the structured breakage is higher severity. traceback from runtime when we log decoder tokens shows attention offsets shift on cached path for some sequences: `kv_start_idx` mismatch for layer 8 in mixed-int8 kernel.
sanjay: i pulled a flamegraph. gist: https://internal.gists/repro/1835551234/flame.svg (stack snippet: attention_forward -> packed_kv_read -> quant_dequant -> softmax).
anya: that chain points to quant dequant rounding inside packed KV read. Could be different scale used when writing vs reading cached kv. Are we using per-head scales?
mike: we switched to per-tensor scaling for speed in the new selector for INT8 to reduce kernel launches. that change is part of the PR. suspect scale mismatch between write path (fp16->quant) and read path (quant->fp16) when cached.
claire: any quick mitigation we can deploy? maybe force fp16 attention kernels when kv-cache enabled until we fix?
sanjay: quick patch: detect kv_cache enabled + quant_mode != pure_fp16 -> prefer fp16 attention kernel. cheap to add and should eliminate misalignments. i'll open a canary PR.
anya: before we do that, can we make a small reproducer that toggles per-head vs per-tensor scale to confirm? i can run targeted eval on 50 prompt seeds.
mike: repro script i used:```bash
# repro loop
for s in {1..50}; do
  python -m rl_eval.run --model redwood-mix-q4_k \
    --prompt-file tests/structured_prompts.jsonl --seed $s \
    --quant-config '{"mode":"mixfp8-int8","scale":"per_tensor"}' \
    --kv-cache true --out results/s.$s.jsonl
done
```
results: with per_tensor scale we see ~8/50 fails, with per_head scale 0/50.
anya: okay that's pretty indicative. per-head scaling seems to avoid the drift. but per-head is slower. how much slower?
perf-bot: per-head-int8 p50 token latency +18% vs per-tensor, throughput -12%.
mike: tradeoff. For correctness we probably need per-head, or at least ensure write/read use same scaling. maybe bug is we applied different quant paths on write vs read for cache.
sanjay: looked at code: write path uses `quantize_tensor(tensor, scale_table[layer])` and read path uses `dequantize(tensor, bake_global_scale)` in some fallback branch introduced by selector. i can repro mismatch by forcing different scale tables.
anya: could be selector chooses a different kernel at read time (because sequence length changed, batch changed) and that kernel expects a different quant layout. when fallback/batch remix happens, cached KV doesn't get converted. we need to store metadata with the cached KV blobs (quant mode, scale type, kernel id).
claire: short-term: sanjay's kernel-force to fp16 for kv-cache is OK for canary. mid-term: store quant metadata with cached KV and add a conversion path on read if needed.
mike: agree. action items: 1) sanjay opens canary PR to prefer fp16 when kv-cache+quant. 2) anya runs 2k-prompt stress with per-head vs per-tensor to quantify failure rate and perf delta. 3) sanjay adds metadata on cached-kv and conversion shim. 4) add eval unit that parses structured outputs under quant modes.
sanjay: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 (WIP) — adds kernel selection override and test.
anya: i'll run the stress tests tomorrow morning and post numbers. can we also run a bisect of the kernel-selector change? maybe it was an earlier commit.
mike: bisect plan: runner `perf-bisect --range ab000..ab12f3 --target tests/structured_prompts.jsonl --metric parse_failures`. assign to me.
claire: note for SRE: if we flip canary to prefer fp16 on kv-cache we should watch cost impact on Dedicated clusters. talk to finance if it rolls into prod.
mike: thanks. any other thoughts?
anya: longer term: we should add an invariant in CI: cached-KV must round-trip quant->dequant->quant equal under all selector paths. add a unit that serializes cached kv and reloads with all supported kernel variants.
sanjay: good idea. i'll add that test.
mike: cool — i'll file the regression ticket and tag eng-ml/eng-runtime. ticket: INF-1978. linking PRs & stress results once available. :thumbsup:
claire: ack. monitoring run in #eng-sre once canary deployed.
anya: thanks team — will update after stress runs.
